analysis.title: FOMC Recap: From the window to the wall…a Dec hike is still our call
key_insights: The FOMC held its policy rate unchanged at an upper bound of 4.00% in October, following a hike in September. The vote was 10-2.
Cleveland Fed President Hammack and Governor Cook dissented in favor of a hike. This was Cook's first dissent since taking office in 2022.
Dallas Fed President Logan and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari dissented for a hike when the Fed held in July. They did not dissent this time.
Natixis says a December hike is likely a foregone conclusion absent a significant shift in the data. Inflation remains a problem, growth is strong and unemployment is stable.

The pause follows NY Fed President Williams and Vice Chair Jefferson implying that consecutive hikes are not urgent. Natixis suggests asset volatility and wobbly tech names may have removed some accommodation between meetings.

The statement upgraded its growth assessment from solid to strong. It added language that more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation.
Natixis reads the added language as giving the FOMC time to see whether the higher-than-expected September inflation print was a one-time increase or the start of a new upward trend.
At the press conference Chair Warsh cited stronger trend growth, record capex and low unemployment. He said it is the FOMC's responsibility to get inflation down.
Warsh said financial conditions have tightened for some businesses and households since September but remain loose on net. He also said energy and related prices have moved higher again.

The FOMC will keep eight meetings per year. In 2027 one meeting will focus only on monetary policy strategy, with no vote or statement. In 2028 two meetings will be strategy-only and six will set policy.
Warsh gave an ambiguous answer when asked why the FOMC did not hike in October. He was skeptical that AI spending is insensitive to interest rates.
Warsh said market participants are more selective about AI-related credit, with some spreads widening. He added that capex strength has extended beyond AI over the past few quarters.
Natixis forecasts one more hike this cycle, in December. The call is contingent on encouraging inflation data and additional concerns about the growth outlook.

Natixis expects domestically generated inflation to slow and core inflation to trend down if tariff and energy price pressures wane. It cites low consumer confidence and flat to negative real wage gains.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held after a September hike. Natixis expects a further 25bp-style step in December only if inflation data cooperates.

macro_indicators.reading: 10-2 (Hammack and Cook dissenting for a hike)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Two dissents favor tightening, which signals a hawkish bias on the committee despite the pause.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike expected (one more hike this cycle)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Natixis' base case, conditional on encouraging inflation data and growth concerns. Natixis calls a December hike likely a foregone conclusion absent a significant data shift.

macro_indicators.reading: Higher than expected, described as unusually noisy
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed wants to learn whether it was a one-time increase or the start of a new upward trend.

risk_factors: Sustainability of AI-related investment, which drives growth disproportionately, is paramount to markets and economic health.
Some AI-related credit spreads are widening as market participants become more selective.
A second inflation upside surprise could keep the Fed hiking.
Tariffs and higher energy costs are non-cyclical price pressures that may not wane.
Low consumer confidence and flat to negative real wage gains could weaken demand and growth.
vol_and_positioning: Natixis says asset volatility and some wobbly tech names in the intermeeting period may have removed a further dose of accommodation, which could explain the pause.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish read: inflation remains a problem, growth is strong, unemployment is stable, and two dissenters wanted a hike now, so a December hike is likely a foregone conclusion.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish read: slower growth from low consumer confidence and flat to negative real wages, plus easing tariff and energy pressures, would bring disinflation and prompt the Fed to avoid overtightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Natixis' December hike call is contingent on encouraging inflation data in the coming months and additional concerns about the growth outlook.
